text: The kitchen smelled like burnt sugar when I walked in. Mom stood at the stove, stirring something dark in the pot. She didn't look up. Outside, the afternoon sun made everything too bright through the window. I asked if she needed help, but she just shook her head. The spoon kept moving in circles. I sat at the table and watched her shoulders, the way they curved forward like she was protecting something. The clock ticked on the wall. A fly landed on the counter, then took off again. Finally, she turned around and smiled, the kind of smile that doesn't reach your eyes. 'It's almost ready,' she said, though neither of us knew what it was supposed to become.
